articles.title: Trump May Ditch Iran Nuclear Deal If Tehran Fully Reopens Strait of Hormuz | Report
articles.description: US President Donald Trump may be shifting his focus from a new nuclear agreement with Iran to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. According to reports, Washington could maintain the current ceasefire and potentially suspend efforts for a new nuclear deal if Iran fully restores shipping through the strategic waterway. Tehran is reportedly demanding sanctions relief, an end to the U.S. naval blockade, the withdrawal of American forces and financial compensation in return. With Hormuz crucial to global energy supplies, the standoff could have major consequences for oil prices, regional security and the future of U.S.-Iran relations.

articles.title: Kash Patel to Moscow? Kremlin-Linked Analyst Says ‘Don’t Come Empty-Handed’
articles.description: Donald Trump’s reported plans for a trip to Russia are raising questions after a Kremlin-linked analyst suggested that FBI Director Kash Patel should not arrive in Moscow “empty-handed.” Patel is reportedly expected to visit Moscow and St. Petersburg in October, where he could meet with Russia’s powerful FSB security service. The unusual trip has fueled speculation about possible U.S.-Russia backchannel discussions and Patel’s potential role as a liaison between the Trump administration and Moscow. Russia has remained tight-lipped about the reported visit, while Patel has highlighted FBI cooperation with Russian law-enforcement agencies on cross-border crime.

articles.title: 'NO TALKS WITH TRUMP!': Iran HUMILIATES U.S., Drops SHOCK List Of Hormuz Conditions
articles.description: Iran has slammed the brakes on direct diplomacy with the United States. Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran will not engage in direct talks, while accusing Washington of violating a June interim agreement. However, messages between the two sides are still being exchanged through intermediaries, he added. The biggest flashpoint remains the Strait of Hormuz. Araghchi said Iran and Oman were in the final stages of an agreement to establish new maritime routes through the strategic waterway. But Tehran insists that finalizing those routes does not mean Hormuz will immediately reopen.
